concurrency_primitives: goroutines, bounded buffered channels, sync.WaitGroup; both datasets processed concurrently (main.go:129-140); per-dataset reader goroutine streams rows into a workers*2 channel consumed by NumCPU workers with private count maps, merged after wg.Wait (processing.go:10-74); worker pool over ~280 neighborhood names for the join (processing.go:78-148)
design_patterns: README claims Pipeline; realized only loosely as stream -> worker pool -> merge -> join -> print, with all five analyses inline in main()
questions: Which neighborhoods have the most 311 service requests? (single dataset)
Which neighborhoods have the most vacant property records? (single dataset)
What is the correlation between neighborhood 311 counts and vacant property counts?
Which neighborhoods have the highest ratio of 311 requests to vacant property records?
Which neighborhoods should city officials prioritize (50/50 normalized 311 + vacant score)?
overview: Three-file single-package Go program: ingestion.go streams CSV neighborhoods into a channel, processing.go runs a worker pool that counts them and a second pool that joins the two count maps, and main.go computes and prints five questions inline. Clean and readable with deterministic ordering, but no tests, no realized design pattern beyond a loose pipeline, and analysis mixed with output.
stakeholder_value: Only the correlation and the 50/50 priority score genuinely combine the datasets; the top-5 lists restate what each source dataset already shows and the requests-per-vacant ratio is dominated by neighborhoods with a single notice. The priority shortlist (Broadway East, Carrollton Ridge, Sandtown-Winchester) is plausible but unnormalized and unfiltered, so a planning office gains little beyond what the vacant-notice counts alone provide.
issues: Two of five questions are single-dataset top-5 lists; Q4 ratio is degenerate (Riverside 5963:1 from one vacant notice).
Worker pool does trivial per-row counting; CSV parsing is sequential per file; join pool is token concurrency.
All five analyses and output live inline in main(); README's Pipeline pattern is only loosely realized.
Prebuilt macOS binary shipped without execute permission and an executable copy was SIGKILLed by macOS; not verifiable (source build graded).
go.mod go 1.27.2 forces a toolchain download on older Go installs.
rationale: Clean build, two bundled real datasets and a successful end-to-end run matching the README earn full marks on build, real_data and runs_results. Partial concurrency (correct pools doing trivial work, sequential parsing), lightly documented memory handling, a small untested single-package design, and shallow questions with two single-dataset items and no named stakeholders account for the deductions. 71/100, C.
